candidates.source_title: Rochdale's seven College Bank tower blocks set to make way for hundreds of new homes
candidates.source_summary: Plans to redevelop the College Bank estate in Rochdale have been confirmed, with hundreds of new 'affordable homes' proposed for the site currently occupied by seven tower blocks.
candidates.source_body_excerpt: Plans to redevelop the College Bank estate in Rochdale have been confirmed, with hundreds of new 'affordable homes' proposed for the site currently occupied by seven tower blocks. Rochdale Boroughwide Housing (RBH) has decided to pursue redevelopment after a review found that refurbishing the existing buildings could cost at least £269 million and take up to 12 years. The decision follows more than a year of discussions involving RBH, Rochdale Council and the Greater Manchester Mayor-led College Bank Task Force. The seven tower blocks, built in the 1960s, contain 766 flats and have been subject to an ongoing rehousing programme since October 2025 because of concerns about their long-term safety. According to RBH, just 78 households have yet to accept an offer of alternative accommodation, with the housing provider expecting all remaining residents to have moved out by summer 2027. The organisation says the rehousing programme will continue regardless of the redevelopment decision. A feasibility study carried out during summer 2025 examined whether the existing buildings could be retained and refurbished. Structural surveys, engineering assessments and financial modelling found that refurbishment would require substantial reconstruction, costing an estimated £388,000 per flat before VAT.

candidates.source_title: The £5.6m plan to deal with costly homeless accommodation in Rochdale
candidates.source_summary: As of the strat of November, there were 387 Rochdale households using temporary accommodation
candidates.source_body_excerpt: Hundreds of families are currently living in temporary accommodation in Rochdale – and it comes at a huge cost to the council. Now the town hall has a £5.6m plan to make sure temporary accommodation is suitable and more cost-effective over the next four years. The local authority has devised a framework that would help them control the types of housing they offer those at risk of homelessness – who can be some of the most vulnerable in society. As of the beginning of November, there are 387 Rochdale households in temporary accommodation, according to council papers. Of these, 250 of are families with children and there 13 families in Bed & Breakfasts and five families in out of borough placements. Click here to get the biggest stories straight to your inbox in our Daily Newsletter The use of hotels and B&Bs is the most expensive provision and is also more likely not to be up to standard, a report found. A higher complexity of need for those using the council’s housing service as well as a decrease in social housing supply in the borough is what has sparked the town hall to take action. The new framework would allow the town hall to have greater oversight and influence over the local supported accommodation. The plan would see the types of accommodation into four ‘Lots’ and is estimated to cost £5.6m over four years. Lot 1 and Lot 2 would incur the largest expense at an estimated £4.9m, because they include B&Bs and nightly paid accommodation for the homeless. Lot 3 would contain homelessness supported accommodation and Lot 4 would be ‘supported pathway housing’ for homeless families and individuals. The framework would allow housing providers to register with the council under one of these ‘lot’ pathways and the local authority would identify whether they meet the required standards. A report read: “While the council’s strategic approach is to minimise and progressively reduce the use of B&B accommodation, these established arrangements provide an important contingency option in emergency and exceptional circumstances where no suitable alternative temporary accommodation is immediately available. “These partnerships provide valuable resilience within the council’s temporary accommodation pathway whilst longer-term, more suitable accommodation solutions are secured.” Rochdale council ’s cabinet will meet next week to discuss and sign off on the plans.

Naimh Mooney has signed for Wigan Warriors under-19s academy as she hopes one day to pull on a first-team jersey. The 16-year-old has overcome mental and physical struggles to reach this point — including tearing her ACL and breaking her collar bone — and believes no one should give up on their dreams. Sporty Naimh had trials for Manchester United’s youth girls before taking up rugby. She joined Rochdale Mayfield ARLFC and then Leigh Miners Rangers Girls, before signing for Wigan. Naimh said: “I have always liked sport and both my parents were into sports when I was growing up — mum was hockey and dad was cricket. “I started playing rugby at 12 and loved it. It gave me a focus and helped with my mental health when I was having major problems at school. “It gave me new ways of seeing things and an outlet for my emotions. Naimh, whose preferred position of half-back, is currently undergoing pre-season training with Wigan’s academy, alongside a barbering course at Oldham College.

candidates.source_body_excerpt: A York City FC player has appeared in court after allegedly punching a Rochdale AFC supporter during a pitch invasion. Hiram Boateng, 30, of Leeds, pleaded not guilty at Manchester Magistrates' Court on Monday to using threatening, abusive or insulting behaviour with intent to cause fear of, or provoke, unlawful violence. The charge relates to an incident involving fans who entered the pitch during the final-day match between the two sides at the Crown Oil Arena on 25 April. York City FC said it was "aware of developments" following the incident and added Boateng, whose trial is due to begin on 23 June 2027, "maintains the full support of everyone at York City". Rochdale supporters entered the pitch during the match after believing their side had secured the National League title. The alleged incident happened during a second pitch invasion later in the game. A spokesperson for York City FC said: "We are aware of developments regarding the incident involving Hiram Boateng during the game against Rochdale in April. "We are continuing to work with him and all the appropriate authorities to address this and to understand the circumstances that led to this. "Hiram maintains the full support of everyone at York City and is a much-valued member of the squad, both on and off the pitch."

candidates.source_title: Ex-MK Dons midfielder in court after York City-Rochdale pitch invasion
candidates.source_summary: The former MK Dons man is facing charges after an altercation with a fan during a pitch invasion
candidates.source_body_excerpt: Midfielder Hiram Boateng has been charged with affray following an on-field incident while playing for York City against Rochdale last April. The ex-MK Dons man has been accused of hitting a Rochdale fan following a pitch invasion during the 1-1 draw which saw City promoted from the National League at their opponents’ expense. There were two pitch invasions during the game - the first when Rochdale scored in the 95th minute, believing they had won the title, before York’s even later equaliser, sparking a second invasion at full-time. It is during the second that Boateng is alleged to have struck the fan. Boateng made 65 appearances in three seasons at Stadium MK. Initially joining the club in the summer of 2019, he also spent a year on loan at Cambridge United before returning to MK1, departing for Mansfield Town in 2022, and leaving for York in 2025. York, now playing in League Two, are managed by ex-Dons head coach Scott Lindsey. The 30-year-old is charged with using threatening, abusive or insulting behaviour with intent to cause fear of or provoke violence, and appeared in magistrates’ court on Monday in Manchester, where no pleas were entered. A club statement said: “We are aware of developments regarding the incident involving Hiram Boateng during the game against Rochdale in April. “We are continuing to work with him and all the appropriate authorities to address this and to understand the circumstances that led to this. “Hiram maintains the full support of everyone at York City and is a much-valued member of the squad, both on and off the pitch.” York City co-owner Matt Uggla took to social media to defend the player, saying: “ A fan runs onto the pitch to deliberately antagonise a player, yet it’s Hiram who ends up facing a criminal charge. “Where’s the accountability for the person who invaded the pitch and provoked the situation? Absolutely ridiculous. “We’re fully behind Hiram.”

candidates.source_body_excerpt: Campaigners fighting to save Rochdale’s College Bank flats from demolition are calling on community leaders to step in and save the landmark tower blocks. Yesterday, Rochdale Boroughwide Housing announced that demolition and redevelopment of the site is the only viable option for the 61-year-old tower blocks known as the Seven Sisters. It said refurbishing them would cost at least £269 million and take up to 12 years — estimated at £388,000 for each of the 766 flats before VAT. RBH said the renovations would add another 50 years to the lifespan of the buildings, while redevelopment would provide 601 homes in a mix of sizes, creating a minimum additional 249 bedrooms, and the properties would last “significantly longer”. Reacting to the news, Greater Manchester Tenants Union said the decision was part of a “managed decline” overseen by the housing provider — a claim RBH denies. GMTU said: “Campaigners and the wider community are very disappointed with the decision to pursue demolition by RBH. “For 10 years the tenants and leaseholders of College Bank have suffered one mistaken decision after another. “RBH claims the decision is based upon ‘a detailed review of all available scenarios’ but it has only allowed for a costing of an overpriced refurbishment plan based upon installing a second staircase in each block of College Bank (under new regulations following the Grenfell disaster).”

Rochdale's Seven Sisters tower blocks, which contain 766 flats, will be replaced by about 600 homes , social landlord Rochdale Boroughwide Housing (RBH) has said. Demolition of the tower blocks was first proposed in 2017 but was ruled out in 2023 after a local campaign against it, but residents began moving out in October 2025 over long-term safety concerns. Roy Kitcher and Christina Hartley, who have lived in one of the blocks for 14 years, said they were left "upset" and "angry". RBH said demolition was the only "realistic and affordable" option. Kitcher said: "It's devastating news - why they want to knock them down, I don't know." The couple are one of 78 households yet to accept an offer of another home. "This is home and I want to stay here, I don't want to be moving out again," Kitcher added.

candidates.source_body_excerpt: After a decade of limbo for residents living in the iconic tower blocks - a decision on the future of the Seven Sisters has been made Residents of the Seven Sisters tower blocks in Rochdale have been left saddened, angered and disappointed after learning their homes are going to be bulldozed. Rochdale Boroughwide Housing (RBH) have made the decision to demolish the 766 flats and replace them with a mix of 601 new flats and townhouses. The decision brings to an end an era of uncertainty for the towers, actually called College Bank, which were first earmarked for demolition a decade ago. What used to be a bustling community on the outskirts of Rochdale town centre now sits silent. That’s because only around 80 households remain from the original 766 since the original demolition announcement 10 years ago. Click here to get the biggest stories straight to your inbox in our Daily Newsletter The uncertainty about the blocks' future has led many tenants to move on. Even hardened campaigners from the Save the Seven Sisters (ST7S) group have gone. The campaigners have fought to stop demolition ever since it was first mentioned in 2016. They want to see the 1960s block refurbished instead. RBH deemed it too expensive and believed it would take too long to refurbish the blocks, so opted to redevelop. They estimated that it would take 12 years to refurbish and cost £269m – around £388,000 per flat.

candidates.source_body_excerpt: Less than 10%of the homes remain occupied. Credit: Google Earth The town’s skyline-defining tower blocks are to be demolished after Rochdale Boroughwide Housing concluded retaining them would be too costly. College Bank, known locally as Seven Sisters, is made up of seven 1960s tower blocks containing 766 bedsits. After years of uncertainty over their future, RBH has decided to pull the buildings down once the last residents have been rehoused by next summer and replace them with around 600 new-build dwellings. The regeneration project will result in a net increase of around 250 bedspaces, according to the housing association. A planning application is expected early next year. The decision to knock down the existing buildings was made after it was calculated that the cost of retrofitting them would be at least £269m – which works out at around 388,000 a flat. A retrofit project would have taken around 12 years to complete and the works would have been good for about 50 years, according to RBH. The new homes would be both cheaper to build and last longer, RBH added.

candidates.source_body_excerpt: Rochdale’s landmark College Bank towers are to be demolished with hundreds of new homes created as part of a major town centre redevelopment. Plans to demolish College Bank were first discussed in 2017 when RBH warned that the buildings were approaching the end of their life. Tenants set up the Save the Seven Sisters campaign and hoped RBH’s partnership with Legal and General Affordable Homes would see the towers restored. In September, 2024, it was announced that the partnership would not continue. Landlord Rochdale Boroughwide Housing said that following a detailed feasibility study which includes structural surveys, engineering assessments, architectural design work and financial modelling, redevelopment is the only option. The housing provider said the findings, which have been ratified by the College Bank Task Force, showed that retaining and refurbishing the blocks would require substantial reconstruction, cost at least £269 million and take up to 12 years to complete. Campaigners wanted the Seven Sisters to be renovated and not demolished It said the cost of refurbishment was estimated at around £388,000 per flat before VAT, and, even after this investment, the homes would have an expected lifespan of about 50 years. It expects the newly built homes to last significantly longer and better meet the current and future housing needs of people in the borough.

Former PC Lenny Cook, of Crow Hill South, Middleton, was dismissed without notice following an Accelerated Misconduct Hearing on Friday, November 13. Greater Manchester Police (GMP) said his conduct was found to amount to gross misconduct and he has now been placed on the College of Policing Barred List, preventing him from serving in policing again. The hearing concerned an incident in Manchester city centre in the early hours of September 23, 2025. According to GMP, police received reports of a disturbance on Peter Street at around 12.41am after members of the public witnessed Cook behaving aggressively towards a woman and grabbing her by the neck. Officers who attended identified Cook and the woman as off-duty police officers, GMP said, and Cook was arrested at the scene. As he was arrested, Cook kicked a firearms officer, who was on duty. candidates.source_body_excerpt: Ignite Fire Festival returns to Rochdale with Christmas lights switch-on Families can enjoy three evenings of glowing fire trails, live circus stunts, and dazzling festive lights without paying a penny to get in. The popular winter showcase will transform local parkland and historic gardens into an illuminated wonderland ahead of the big seasonal switch-on. Visitors can wander through a brand new multi-sensory trail exploring the human body using heat, sound, and special effects. Live drumming groups, flame-cooked street food, and stalls run by young local makers will also keep crowds entertained throughout the weekend. Most of the outdoor route is step-free, making it easy for families with pushchairs and wheelchair users to explore the glowing displays together. Organisers hope the lively celebration will bring neighbours together and provide a magical start to the winter holidays. Taking centre stage at this year's Ignite Fire Festival is 'BODY', an immersive outdoor installation making its north-west debut after touring around the world. Created by outdoor arts specialists Walk the Plank, the trail guides guests through six glowing zones representing the hidden heat and energy inside the human body. Behind Rochdale Town Hall, a sparkling Fire Garden will light up the slopes with pyrotechnics alongside live fire-spinning feats from Travelling Light Circus and local community performers. The 20-strong drumming group Drum Machine and Skylight Circus Arts will also return to bring energetic music and movement to the evening crowds. Sue Smith, cabinet member for communities and co-operation at Rochdale Borough Council, said: "Ignite is the perfect way to kick off the festive season, bringing together spectacular entertainment, dazzling displays and magical moments for all ages. Bigger and brighter than ever this year, it's the ultimate build-up to our Christmas lights switch-on." Visitors can warm up with flame-cooked food including brisket, macaroni cheese, and bratwurst, or browse handmade gifts at a nightly Teenage Market. On Friday, November 20 from 5.30pm to 7.30pm, families can also walk over to Clay & Glaze on Drake Street to paint a fire or dragon-themed mug for £10.

candidates.source_title: Police probe ‘horrific spate of attacks against hospice’ - Rochdale Times
candidates.source_summary: Thieves have caused thousands of pounds worth of damage after four break-ins at Springhill Hospice shops in the past two weeks.
candidates.source_body_excerpt: Thieves have caused thousands of pounds worth of damage after four break-ins at Springhill Hospice shops in the past two weeks. The hospice’s home and furniture shop at Jacksons Corner, Molesworth Street, Rochdale, was targeted for the third time yesterday, after a break-in at the Oldham Road shop on Saturday morning. The weekend’s incidents follow two previous break-in attempts at the furniture shop in the past fortnight. The hospice shared: “A brick was thrown through the window of our home and furniture shop, making it the fourth break in attempt across our shops in the past two weeks. “The police continue to investigate this horrific spate of attacks against our hospice. “We’re asking our community to please be extra vigilant. If you see anything suspicious around our shops, particularly overnight, please report it to the police. “These break ins have resulted in significant damage to both of our shops which will cost the hospice thousands of pounds to repair, as well as days of lost trading because of shop closures. candidates.source_title: Today marks 215 years since the birth of the 'greatest master of English oratory' John Bright, influential Rochdale-born statesman
candidates.source_summary: Today marks the 215th anniversary of the birth of the free-trade advocate and abolitionist John Bright (1811-1889). Celebrated and lauded by many, including Abraham Lincoln and Lord Salisbury, John Bright is arguably Rochdale's greatest statesman
candidates.source_body_excerpt: Today marks the 215th anniversary of the birth of the free-trade advocate and abolitionist John Bright (1811-1889). Celebrated and lauded by many, including Abraham Lincoln and Lord Salisbury, John Bright is arguably Rochdale's greatest statesman John Bright was a statesman from Rochdale, belonging initially to the Radical Party until its merger into the Liberal Party in 1859. He was lauded by many, Lord Salisbury, former Prime Minister three times over, upon Bright's death, remarked that "he (Bright) was the greatest master of English oratory that this generation has produced, or I may perhaps say several generations back." Abraham Lincoln had a portrait of John Bright in his office, and among the items retrieved from his pocket upon his assassination, was a testimony from Bright supporting the re-election of the President. Bright became an MP for 4 separate constituencies, and served as a cabinet minister on three separate occasions, all under Liberal Prime Minister William Gladstone. Bright was an abolitionist, and supported fugitive slave Frederick Douglass both spread his story, and become a free man. Bright was a supporter of the co-operative movement, and introduced Douglass to crowds almost a thousand strong in Rochdale wanting to hear him speak of his story as a slave in America. Frederick Douglass notably spoke in the Public Room on Baillie Street on October 10th 1846, just a three minute walk from where the first co-operative store was opened by the Rochdale Pioneers two years prior. Bright contributed a third of the cost to buy Douglass' freedom from slavery, and, in 1847, Douglass went back to America a free man. Douglass was a regular guest at 'One Ash', the home of John Bright, and he stayed there the night before he was to leave England for America as a free man for the first time. Douglass noted that, relating to the hospitality of Bright “I was, besides, a welcome guest at the home of Mr. Bright in Rochdale and treated as a friend and brother among his brothers and sisters.” Douglass went on to become an influential abolitionist and supporter of women's suffrage, being the only black attendant to the first women's rights convention, and the first black candidate for the vice-presidency under the first female candidate for the presidency. Bright was known for his staunch advocacy for free-trade policies, evidenced through his role in the Anti-Corn Law League, which he founded alongside his friend (and later MP for Rochdale) Richard Cobden. The Corn Laws were a set of mercantilist/protectionist tariffs and trade restrictions levied on imported wheat in an attempt to protect national farming interests. This caused the prices for common wheat products like bread to rise, disproportionately negatively impacting the urban working class. Bright joined forces with Cobden with the creation of one of the first nationwide successful pressure groups, officially in 1836, but functionally in 1838. In 1846, the Conservative Prime Minister Robert Peel led the successful battle for repeal, and the success of the pressure group established by Bright and Cobden was a primary reason for the eventual repealing of these laws, symbolising a shift in policy from mercantilism/protectionism to free trade. This was incredibly controversial, and the conservatives broadly didn't support this, with Peel relying on the support of the Whigs to pass the repeal of the Corn Laws. Peel resigned the very day that the repeal passed through parliament. Critics of the repeal of the Corn Laws, including Benjamin Disraeli, saw that the repeal of these laws caused the ruin of British agriculture, yet supporters of the repeal of these laws saw that the urban working class were baring an unfair load as a result of the expensive food prices. Benjamin Disraeli opted not to reinstate the Corn Laws for this reason, seeing the value of free-trade policies and the benefit that the repeal of the law had on the urban working class. Rochdale statesman John Bright, and former Rochdale MP Richard Cobden were two of the main pioneers for the repeal of the Corn Laws, and of the extension of free-trade policies in Britain. Two famous terms have been attributed to Bright, one being the idiom to 'flog a dead horse', and the other being in relation to England being the 'mother of all parliaments'. Bright has two statues, one near Manchester Town Hall, and the other in Broadfield Park in Rochdale. They were both unveiled in 1891, but the latter was moved from the initial placing of the Town Hall Square to the park in 1933. The inscriptions on the statue in Broadfield Park note Bright as 'Rochdale's greatest townsman', accompanied by quotes from the 'master of English oratory'.

candidates.source_title: Homeless support steps up as winter sweeps in – Rochdale Borough Council
candidates.source_summary: People experiencing homelessness across the borough are being provided with extra support as cold weather sweeps in.
candidates.source_body_excerpt: People experiencing homelessness across Rochdale borough are being provided with extra support as the cold weather sweeps in. Temperatures are closely monitored and, when severe weather conditions are forecast, the support already available to people sleeping rough significantly increases across all townships. Additional outreach workers are now on the streets during the day and throughout the night, engaging with anyone sleeping rough and helping them access accommodation and support services. Bed capacity across accommodation services has been increased, while community support hubs will extend their opening hours during periods of severe weather. The hubs provide access to hot food and drinks, shower and laundry facilities, welfare support, health services and more to help people move away from rough sleeping and into longer-term accommodation. In addition, housing staff will continue to link in with the new Safe Haven site in Rochdale Town Hall Square. The Safe Haven is a trailer which parks in this area every Saturday between 10pm and 3am and is fully staffed with clinical and non-clinical teams to support anyone who is on a night out and feeling vulnerable. The teams supporting the homeless, including the council and its many partners, will continue to work with the safe haven team to ensure that anyone who is going into the haven because they need a bed for the night will be supported into accommodation. Councillor Danny Meredith, cabinet member for housing and regeneration, said: “Council teams and partners work all year round to support our most vulnerable residents, but we know they are more at risk in cold weather. By significantly stepping up the support at this time of year, we will ensure that nobody who wants a bed will be without one. “This 24-hour response supports people in immediate crisis and that’s really important, but we also offer long term support because ultimately, we want people to be able to build a life away from the streets. As well as provision to help the person, like support with jobs, training and mental health, we’re also creating new move-on accommodation to help people who are working towards a permanent home, and in the longer term are working to create more affordable housing.”

candidates.source_body_excerpt: Photo © ALF Recruit - winner of New Business of the Year and Business of the Year - turnover under £1m Businesses and individuals from across Rochdale borough have been recognised at the 13th annual Rochdale Business Awards. The awards recognise achievements ranging from business growth and customer service to sustainability, community engagement and the development of the next generation of Rochdale talent. The winners of 12 categories from Apprentice of the Year to Business of the Year were announced during the ceremony at Rochdale Town Hall on Friday. Wheeldon Bros Waste Ltd won Sustainable Environmental Business of the Year, while Performance Doorset Solutions Ltd took Business of the Year for turnover over £5m. Conor Weldon of Salt Separation Services Ltd was named Apprentice of the Year, and the company also won Employer of the Year. ALF Recruit won two awards, as New Business of the Year and Business of the Year for turnover under £1m. Councillor Neil Emmott, Leader of Rochdale Borough Council, said: “Rochdale has a thriving and ambitious business community, with organisations across the borough creating jobs, investing in our towns and bringing new ideas and opportunities. The Business Awards are a fantastic opportunity to recognise the people and businesses driving that success. “From major developments at Kingsway and the reopening of Heywood Civic to the growing profile of our towns as places to live, work and visit, there is plenty of positive momentum across the borough. Supporting businesses to grow and recognising their contribution is an important part of that. “Congratulations to all our winners and finalists. Your achievements make a real difference to Rochdale, and we are proud that you have chosen our borough as the place to build and grow your businesses.”

candidates.source_title: RBH sets out future plans for College Bank
candidates.source_summary: Read more about the future of College Bank
candidates.source_body_excerpt: Hundreds of new safe, sustainable and affordable homes are set to be built on the site of College Bank in Rochdale. This decision by the Rochdale Boroughwide Housing (RBH) Board was made after more than a year of working together with our partners in the College Bank Task Force, and follows a detailed review of all available scenarios. There is now a clear route ahead to redevelop the area, on which the seven 1960s tower blocks currently stand, and create a neighbourhood that meets the needs of current and future residents. We will now begin the process of seeking the necessary planning approvals. This decision does not change the ongoing rehousing programme. Customers have already been moving out of College Bank since October 2025, due to safety concerns, and our priority remains supporting every remaining customer to find a home that is right for them. Amanda Newton, Chief Executive, said: "Today marks an important step forward for College Bank and for the future of housing in Rochdale. "College Bank has been home to generations of Rochdalians, and we recognise the important place the blocks hold in many people's memories. I want to thank our customers for the patience, honesty and resilience they have shown throughout what has been a long and difficult process. "This decision gives us a way forward together and allows us to focus on the opportunities ahead. This includes creating hundreds of new, safe, affordable homes on the site that meet Rochdale's current and future housing needs, while continuing to support our existing customers every step of the way.” Only 78 households out of the 766 flats across the seven blocks have yet to accept an offer for a new home, after customers began moving out of their homes in October last year because of concerns about the long-term safety of the blocks.

candidates.source_body_excerpt: YORK City celebrated a first away win of the season as they came away from old foes Rochdale with a 1-0 win. Ollie Pearce’s goal and some last-ditch defending earned the three points for York at the same place they won promotion last April. The Press’ Gabriel Ramsey was the Crown Oil Arena on Saturday and provides the match stats and his player ratings. Lindsey said it was a ‘real mature’ performance from young goalkeeper McNally pre-match, and he’s summed it up perfectly. Playing against seasoned pro’s like Ian Henderson and Aden Flint, McNally guarded his goal superbly. He made some top, top saves too and earned his clean sheet. Felix worked hard down the right and put in some dangerous crosses. He was unlucky that he didn’t find a yellow shirt on them, before being subbed off with 23 minutes to go. Outstanding. A captain’s performance from Fallowfield, who didn’t put a foot wrong all afternoon. He defended impeccably, was rarely beaten down his side and made two goal line clearances. Potentially his best ever performance in a City shirt. Johnson was immense. He absolutely pocketed Dajaune Brown, who had his chances, but Johnson did enough each time to put him off. He won his battles and was absolutely integral at the heart of the defence. It’s easy to forget sometimes just how young he is! Kitching was impressive down the left. He defended strongly and was equally as impressive in an attacking sense, getting City up the pitch and out of tight situations at times.

candidates.source_title: There are ‘serious failings’ in how Bury council manages its social housing, a government watchdog has warned
candidates.source_summary: Outcomes in safety and accountability were judged to be particularly poor, with the Regulator of Social Housing saying it cannot be sure the town hall is meeting its legal duties.
candidates.source_body_excerpt: Outcomes in safety and accountability were judged to be particularly poor, with the Regulator of Social Housing saying it cannot be sure the town hall is meeting its legal duties. The council owns around 7,600 homes with some 300 of these managed by an external agency. It was the council’s first inspection under the regulatory framework and it was awarded a C3 rating – the second lowest outcome. The council took its housing services back into direct management in 2024 as it began to wind down social housing provider Six Town Housing (STH). It is in the process of consulting on the future of the remaining around 100 homes managed by STH, with a recent report recommending that these too be brought under the council control. The council believes that will offer ‘greater long-term stability’ for tenants, with alternatives being to sell them on. Among the concerns raised by inspectors were overdue fire safety remedial actions, with 2,800 outstanding at the time of the inspection. While most were assessed as being low to medium risk, the Regulator of Social Housing said there was a ‘lack of clarity’ about the time taken to complete them. The council also could not show it was meeting the ‘legally required timescales’ to investigate, identify and repair hazards such as damp and mould. Awaab’s Law came into effect in October 2025, named in memory of two-year-old boy Awaab Ishak, who tragically died in 2020. Awaab died after prolonged exposure to mould in his Rochdale flat. The new law requires social housing landlords to investigate hazard reports, including of mould, within 10 working days. If the issue is judged to be a ‘significant hazard’, safety work must be completed within five working days, or 24 hours for an ’emergency hazard’. Any further work required must be carried out within a ‘reasonable’ time.

candidates.source_title: Man who died in flat fire named
candidates.source_summary: A man who died in a flat fire in Middleton has been named as David Mills.
candidates.source_body_excerpt: A man who died in a flat fire in Middleton has been named as David Mills. Emergency services rushed to a block on Baguley Crescent shortly afterem 2.30pm on Saturday (November 7) after a blaze broke out in a first-floor flat. Three fire engines attended the scene, close to the border with Prestwich, with firefighters using breathing apparatus to extinguish the flames. Sadly, a man died at the scene. He has now been identified as 67-year-old David Steven Mills. Police are appealing for help tracing his next of kin. In a statement posted on social media, GMP said: “Do you know the next of kin of a man from #Middleton? David Steven Mills, 67, sadly passed away at his address on Baguley Crescent, #Middelton on 07/11/2026. “There are believed to be no suspicious circumstances surrounding his death. Anyone with information about David’s next of kin should contact the Police Coroner’s Office on 0161 856 8555.” The 67-year-old was described by locals as ‘a very kind man’, ‘a gentleman’ and ‘a friend of the community’. Margaret Moulding, who lived across from Mr Mills, said: “He was a very helpful man. He was very kind and it’s very sad.

candidates.source_title: Old office block in Rochdale will be turned into apartments
candidates.source_summary: An empty office block on the outskirts of Rochdale town centre will be converted into apartments. St James Place, on Yorkshire Street, will be transformed into 21 new apartments.
candidates.source_body_excerpt: An empty office block on the outskirts of Rochdale town centre will be converted into apartments. St James Place, on Yorkshire Street, will be transformed into 21 new apartments. After sitting empty for eight years, developer Alam Investments has been granted planning permission to breathe new life into it. The proposal will create a mix of one and two-bedroom flats each with its own living, dining and kitchen space. Only internal changes are planned for the building, so it would be a ‘sensitive and appropriate reuse of the building’, according to developers. Although St James Place isn’t a historically significant building itself, it did house the Socialist Institute when it was built in the 1990s. A heritage statement was required for this planning application due to the Grade II-listed St Mary’s Ukrainian Catholic Church being within close proximity. Planning papers read: “The building has been vacant for approximately eight years and is in need of investment and reuse. “The proposed scheme will bring the property back into productive use, provide much-needed housing in a sustainable location, and contribute positively to the vitality and regeneration of Rochdale town centre.” Add Roch Valley Radio as a preferred source on Google News to see more of our local reporting Do you have a story for us? candidates.source_title: Fire festival returns ahead of Christmas lights switch-on - Rochdale Times
candidates.source_summary: Final preparations are under way for nest week's Ignite Fire Festival and Christmas lights switch-on.
candidates.source_body_excerpt: Final preparations are under way for nest week’s Ignite Fire Festival and Christmas lights switch-on. Ignite Fire Festival, sponsored by car supermarket The Trade Centre UK, will be transforming the square and gardens around Rochdale Town Hall, including the new pathways and parkland on Broadfield Slopes from Friday, November 20 to Sunday, November 22. This free night-time event will open from 5pm to 8pm, delivering a magical trail of fire, lights and sound. Organiser Rochdale Development Agency says this year will be the best yet with new dazzling trails and attractions. Immersive night-time trail BODY will take centre stage, bringing visitors on a journey through six zones of the human body using fire, light, sound and special effects. The multi-sensory experience is the most ambitious fire and light installation yet from multi-award-winning outdoor arts specialists Walk the Plank, and Ignite will be its north-west premiere, after having previously travelled over the globe, from Ireland to Canada. Audiences can expect to be mesmerised on a dramatic, spellbinding journey as they walk through the glowing embers of human metabolism — the silent furnace that keeps us alive, continuously generating heat to power all the body’s functions. Using cutting-edge technology, the experience will entertain and educate, providing a deeper understanding of what lies beneath. There will also be a Fire Garden providing extra sparkle, illuminating slopes and gardens behind Rochdale Town Hall with pyrotechnics, transforming it into a place of beauty. Back again for 2026 is Drum Machine — the 20-strong drumming collective who will be bringing their dance floor grooves and stomping tunes to the festival. Also returning are Fireflies as part of the Culture Co-op programme with Rochdale’s Skylight Circus Arts.

candidates.source_title: Ollie Pearce goal secures maximum points for York at Rochdale - Wilts and Gloucestershire Standard
candidates.source_summary: Ollie Pearce goal secures maximum points for York at Rochdale Wilts and Gloucestershire Standard
candidates.source_body_excerpt: York City tasted victory on the ground where they secured promotion from the National League last season as Ollie Pearce’s goal gave them a 1-0 win at the Crown Oil Arena. Rochdale started brightly, with Dajaune Brown’s header cleared off the line by Harry Boyes six minutes in. On the stroke of half-time, Glenn Middleton was presented with a one-on-one opportunity only for York goalkeeper Alfie McNally to read his attempted dink finish and collect the ball comfortably. In between, the Minstermen had the better of the opening 45 minutes as Hiram Boateng’s effort deflected narrowly wide and Alex Hunt’s rising drive from 20 yards thumped an upright. McNally had to scramble across his goalline to save Brown’s 50th-minute header, and within five minutes the visitors had the lead when Pearce pounced and diverted the ball beyond Sam Waller and into the net. Aden Flint saw an 80th-minute header cleared off the line as Rochdale threatened an equaliser before McNally denied Ian Henderson and Ryan East as York resisted late home pressure.

On the stroke of half-time, Glenn Middleton was presented with a one-on-one opportunity only for York goalkeeper Alfie McNally to read his attempted dink finish and collect the ball comfortably. In between, the Minstermen had the better of the opening 45 minutes as Hiram Boateng’s effort deflected narrowly wide and Alex Hunt’s rising drive from 20 yards thumped an upright. McNally had to scramble across his goalline to save Brown’s 50th-minute header, and within five minutes the visitors had the lead when Pearce pounced and diverted the ball beyond Sam Waller and into the net. Aden Flint saw an 80th-minute header cleared off the line as Rochdale threatened an equaliser before McNally denied Ian Henderson and Ryan East as York resisted late home pressure.

candidates.source_summary: Parents who have children starting primary school next September are being reminded to apply for their child’s school place before Friday, January 15, 2027.
candidates.source_body_excerpt: Parents who have children starting primary school next September are being reminded to apply for their child’s school place before Friday, January 15, 2027. While it is two months away, Rochdale Council is warning that hundreds of families still miss this important deadline. In 2026, 216 parents submitted a late primary school application. This led to more than a third of those children (37%) missing out on their first preferred school as a result when reception started this September. In comparison, 89% of those who submitted an application on time secured their preferred school. Cllr Rachel Massey, cabinet member for children’s services and education, said: “We know life is busy for families, especially when your children are a lot younger, but it is so important to get your school applications in on time. READ MORE: Residents asked to help families in need with Christmas toy appeal “While the deadline is in the new year, January will be here before we know it, so I urge all families to get their applications in as soon as they can to give your child the best possible chance of securing their preferred primary school.”

candidates.source_body_excerpt: A hard-hitting warning has been issued about the dangers of illegal e-bikes and e-scooters as Christmas approaches. Greater Manchester Police and its partners are urging families to think carefully before buying off-road bikes, illegal e-bikes and e-scooters as Christmas gifts, warning that vehicles used unlawfully could be seized and destroyed — or lead to tragedy. The warning comes as part of Operation Hurricane, GMP’s coordinated crackdown on the anti-social and dangerous use of off-road bikes, e-bikes and quad bikes across Greater Manchester. One family which knows the devastating consequences they can cause is that of Jacob Calland, who died after being hit by a car while he was a passenger on an e-scooter when it went through a red light in Wythenshawe in March this year. He died from his injuries eight days later. Jacob’s mother, Carly Calland, said: “No words will ever be able to describe the pain caused by Jacob’s death. My heart has been smashed into a thousand pieces and there is nothing that can be done to fix it. My life is a living nightmare. “I climbed into the hospital bed to cuddle him and I fell asleep holding him. When I woke up, it was time to turn off the machines. I told Jacob I loved him just before he passed away. My baby boy was gone forever. “He won’t sit his GCSEs, he won’t have his sweet sixteen birthday party, he won’t go to his school prom. He won’t be able to follow his dreams. He won’t get married and won’t have children. His life ended the moment that collision happened.” The e-scooter rider, who was 14 at the time, received an 18-month youth referral order and a five-year driving ban after pleading guilty to causing death by dangerous driving, causing death by driving unlicensed, and causing death by driving uninsured.
